subject: History
description: Tilak, Bose, Bhagat Singh, Azad, slogans

questions.stem: The slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it' was given by:
questions.explanation: Tilak (1856-1920), called 'Lokmanya', popularised this slogan during his trial in 1908. The trio of Lala Lajpat Rai, Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal ('Lal-Bal-Pal') led the Extremist wing of the Congress from 1905. Tilak also founded two newspapers — Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English). Subhas Bose's famous slogan was 'Give me blood and I shall give you freedom'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Subhas Chandra Bose organised which military force during the Second World War to fight the British?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Army (INA / Azad Hind Fauj) was originally raised by Mohan Singh from Indian POWs in Japanese-held Singapore (1942) and then reorganised by Subhas Chandra Bose from 1943. It fought alongside the Japanese at Imphal and Kohima. Bose also proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind) on 21 October 1943. The HSRA was Bhagat Singh's revolutionary group; the Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco; the Khudai Khidmatgars were Abdul Ghaffar Khan's non-violent corps.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were hanged by the British on:
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh, Shivaram Rajguru and Sukhdev Thapar were executed by hanging at Lahore Jail on 23 March 1931 for the killing of Assistant Superintendent of Police J. P. Saunders (1928) — itself a retaliation for the death of Lala Lajpat Rai after a police lathi-charge. 23 March is observed in India as Shaheed Diwas (Martyrs' Day). 13 April 1919 was the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

questions.stem: Chandrashekhar Azad shot himself to avoid capture at a park now named after him, in:
questions.explanation: Azad shot himself on 27 February 1931 at Alfred Park, Allahabad (renamed Chandrashekhar Azad Park after Independence). He had sworn never to be captured alive by the British. Leader of the HSRA (Hindustan Socialist Republican Association) after 1928. He had earlier been involved in the Kakori train action (1925) and the Saunders killing (1928). now Prayagraj.

questions.stem: The famous slogan 'Inquilab Zindabad' is most closely associated with:
questions.explanation: 'Inquilab Zindabad' ('Long live the revolution') was coined by the Urdu poet Hasrat Mohani and was popularised by Bhagat Singh and his comrades — they shouted it when they threw leaflets and low-intensity bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly on 8 April 1929. Gandhi's calls were 'Do or Die' (Quit India, 1942) and 'Karo ya Maro'. Bose — 'Jai Hind', 'Tum mujhe khoon do'.

questions.stem: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi died fighting the British near which town in 1858?
questions.explanation: Rani Lakshmibai — Manikarnika Tambe, born in Varanasi — led the defence of Jhansi during the 1857 revolt, fled to Kalpi after the city fell (April 1858), and finally died fighting Hugh Rose's forces near Gwalior on 18 June 1858. She had captured Gwalior Fort with Tatya Tope a few weeks earlier. Subhadra Kumari Chauhan's poem 'Khoob ladi mardani woh to Jhansi wali rani thi' immortalised her story.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on 13 April 1919 in which city?
questions.explanation: On the Baisakhi festival (13 April 1919), Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to open fire on an unarmed crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of local leaders. Hundreds were killed (official British count 379; Indian estimates exceed 1,000). Udham Singh shot Michael O'Dwyer (who had endorsed the action as Punjab Lt-Governor) in London, 1940.
